result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Comparison.identical]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} | Pointblank description: Whether the tables match under the comparison settings. twitter-card: title: >- [Comparison.identical]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} | Pointblank description: Whether the tables match under the comparison settings. title: >- [Comparison.identical]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Whether the tables match under the comparison settings. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Whether the tables match under the comparison settings. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [Comparison.identical]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} A comparison is identical if the schema check passed (see [`schema_ok`](`pointblank.Comparison.schema_ok`)) and no test unit failed. This is the single answer to "are these tables the same?", and it's also the truth value of the comparison, so `if comparison:` is the same as `if comparison.identical:`. "Identical" is relative to the settings given to [`compare()`](`pointblank.compare`). Columns left out with `columns=` aren't checked, values within `tolerance=` count as equal, values are compared after any `normalize=` operations, and with `schema="common"`, the tables can have different columns. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Here, a reporting table stores the readings rounded to one decimal place. ::: {#6980150f .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb import polars as pl raw = pl.DataFrame({"station": ["S1", "S2", "S3"], "temp": [12.14, 14.02, 9.81]}) rounded = pl.DataFrame({"station": ["S1", "S2", "S3"], "temp": [12.1, 14.0, 9.8]}) pb.compare(raw, rounded, keys="station").identical ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` False ``` ::: ::: An exact comparison finds every row changed. Allowing for the rounding with `tolerance=` makes the tables match: ::: {#2fa08a47 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} comparison = pb.compare(raw, rounded, keys="station", tolerance={"temp": 0.05}) comparison.identical ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` True ``` ::: ::: Since a comparison has the same truth value, it can be used directly in a condition: ::: {#3995c3bd .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} if comparison: print("The rounded table matches the raw readings.") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` The rounded table matches the raw readings. ``` ::: ::: A result of `True` here means "the same within 0.05 degrees", not "exactly the same". The settings belong with the result, and the comparison report lists them in its header.
